I am 69 years old. I have worked my land in Quzhou for 50 years, since I was a young girl carrying water for my father. I never went to school one day. I cannot read, but I know this soil with my hands and my feet. I have 12 mu total: 9 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, and 3 mu I plant cotton because I have always grown cotton and the buyer still comes to our village. Seven people live in my house. My sons work in factories in Handan and send money home, so I can buy fertilizer and diesel, but every yuan is still sweat.

I do not read books and I do not trust new talk unless I saw it work on someone else's field. If Old Zhang's wheat looks thick and yellow-green, I copy what Old Zhang does. Last year I put one full bag — 100 jin, 50 kg — of that 15-15-15 compound fertilizer on each mu of wheat before sowing, and then in March I spread 80 jin of urea on top. My wheat gave me nearly 1000 jin per mu. This year I will do the exact same. Better to use a little too much than to risk a thin crop. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is only money.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary-tilled before sowing and used improved seeds from the village shop, the same kind everyone plants. I will irrigate three times from my well: once before winter if the earth is dry, once when the wheat joints in spring, and once when the ears come out. I spray twice — herbicide right after sowing, and one more time in spring for aphids.

After wheat harvest in June, I have no time to rest. I hire the tractor man to rotary-till fast and plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid maize, same as my neighbors. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer — 50 jin, 25 kg — per mu at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I top-dress with 70 jin of urea per mu. Maize is hungry and the summer is hot. I irrigate twice, three times if the drought is bad. Two sprays: one for weeds, one for corn borer when I see the moths.

For cotton on my 3 mu, I plough deep in April because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant improved cotton seeds. I put one bag of compound per mu as base. Then when the flowers open, I spread urea twice — 40 jin each time — and I also buy that red potassium fertilizer, 30 jin per mu, because two years ago I saw Li Mazi's cotton bolls grow fat after he used it, so now I use it too. Cotton drinks water; I irrigate three times. But the real work is spraying. I spray four times for bollworm. If you are lazy with spray, the worms eat your whole year.

I expect my wheat to yield about 485 kg per mu, my maize about 570 kg per mu, and my cotton about 240 kg of seed cotton per mu. If the well does not run dry and the weather is fair, it will be a decent year.
